about.title: Vallejo Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Nineteen people died on Vallejo's roads in 2025, according to final public-record data for the city. Behind each of those numbers is a household in Solano County that is now sorting through funeral arrangements, unpaid bills, and a silence that no paperwork can fill. Collisions in Vallejo cluster along Sonoma Boulevard, I-80, Broadway Street and Tennessee Street, and reports tend to rise on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m., when commuters and weekend traffic overlap. A wrongful death claim is a civil matter, entirely separate from any criminal case the district attorney may or may not pursue. It exists so a family can recover funeral and burial costs, the financial support the person would have provided, and compensation for the love, companionship and guidance that were taken. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that listens to your situation and connects you with an independent attorney who works on contingency, so nothing is owed unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: What a Vallejo Family Should Know Before Filing

items.title: Standing is limited under California law
items.desc: A spouse or registered domestic partner and children have the first right to bring the claim, followed by certain dependents and heirs. An attorney can confirm who in your family is eligible so the case is filed correctly from the start.

items.title: Two years, sometimes less
items.desc: California gives most families two years from the date of death to file. If a public agency may share responsibility, such as for a road or a government vehicle, the window to give notice is far shorter, which is why timing matters in Vallejo cases.

items.title: Recoverable losses go beyond the funeral
items.desc: Claims can include burial expenses, the income and support your loved one would have contributed, and the loss of their companionship and guidance. The civil claim moves independently of any criminal charges.

items.question: My family member was killed in a crash on I-80 near Vallejo. Does it matter that a criminal case is pending?
items.answer: Not for your right to file. A wrongful death claim is a civil action brought by the family, while a criminal case is brought by the state, and the two proceed on separate tracks. The outcome of one does not decide the other, though evidence gathered by investigators can sometimes be useful. An attorney can request records and preserve evidence while the criminal process unfolds.

items.question: Who is allowed to bring a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: The law puts a surviving spouse or domestic partner and the children first in line. If there are none, certain dependents and heirs who relied on the person financially may be able to file. Because eligibility can get complicated in blended or extended families, it is worth having an attorney sort it out early.

items.question: How long do Solano County families have to act?
items.answer: The general deadline is two years from the date of death, not from the date of the crash or diagnosis. If a city, county, or state agency could be partly at fault, a formal claim usually has to be presented within six months, and missing it can end the case. Reaching out sooner gives your attorney time to gather what is needed without rushing you.
